hypothesis.name: conditional_structural_added_value
hypothesis.statement: The incremental value of structural accessibility increases when structural information remains novel relative to the frozen reference model and when the structural representation is updated at the spatiotemporal scale of the response.

moderators.low: reference lacks explicit landscape-specific connectivity/path/resistance representation beyond local environment and simple source distance
moderators.high: reference contains an explicit landscape-specific connectivity/path/current-flow/resistance representation frozen without heldout leakage

moderators.aligned: structural state is recomputed prospectively before each response unit using only information available before that unit
moderators.misaligned: a static structural representation is reused across response occasions whose ecological state may change

prospective_test.outcome: candidate_minus_reference heldout predictive loss under a common endpoint-specific loss metric
prospective_test.primary_prediction: benefit concentrated in low-reference-saturation plus response-aligned endpoints
prospective_test.minimum_design_goal: obtain representation across the two moderator axes rather than maximizing endpoint count

prohibited: claim that historical five-system contrast causally identifies either moderator
compare A-Islands concordance magnitude directly with log-loss deltas
infer mobility or life-history causation from endpoint signs
retroactively alter any closed endpoint classification
select future endpoints after viewing predictive outcomes
